note: Draft data for the cards that act on Domains. No pictures. 'cost' is the cost the test games support (results.txt); 'costTested' is the cost the card has in cards-places.js, where the games started from, when the two differ. 'verdict' says whether the card is worth having. 'sure': 3 well attested, 2 the usual account, 1 a story told about the person, and the sentence says so.

cards.does: look at the top of your stack for a Domain for your Gate or Outpost
cards.tx: When Pachacuti arrives, look at the top three Domains of your stack. You may lay one of them at your Gate or your Outpost in place of the Domain that is there. Put the others under your stack.
cards.fact: He turned the small kingdom of Cusco into the Inca empire and rebuilt its capital in stone, and Machu Picchu was most likely built as his estate.
cards.reads as: Land: a ruler who chooses where his people build.
cards.line: Legacy Line from Machu Picchu and from Qhapaq Ñan

cards.does: look through your whole stack for a Domain for your Gate or Outpost
cards.tx: When Al-Idrisi arrives, you may look through your whole Domain stack, choose one Domain and lay it at your Gate or your Outpost in place of the Domain that is there. Then shuffle your stack.
cards.fact: At the court of Roger II in Palermo he spent some fifteen years questioning travellers, and in 1154 he finished a map of the known world with a book describing every part of it.
cards.reads as: Routes: knowing the land, the map that shows every Domain there is.

cards.tx: When Constantine arrives, you may turn up the top Domain of your stack and lay it at the Crossroads in place of the Domain that is there.
cards.fact: In 330 he made the old Greek town of Byzantium, where Europe meets Asia, his new capital, and it was called Constantinople after him.
cards.reads as: Law: a new capital moves the seat of government.

cards.does: force the other player to replace the Domain at their Gate or Outpost
cards.tx: When William arrives at the other player's Gate or Outpost, you may have the Domain there discarded. The other player lays the top Domain of their stack in its place.
cards.fact: After he won at Hastings in 1066 he gave the land of England to his own followers, and his great survey of 1086, the Domesday Book, shows almost none of it still in English hands.

cards.does: bring back a Domain that was discarded
cards.tx: When Christopher Wren arrives, you may take a Domain from your Domain discard pile and lay it at your Gate or your Outpost in place of the Domain that is there.
cards.fact: After the Great Fire of London in 1666 he rebuilt St Paul's Cathedral and more than fifty of the city's churches.
cards.reads as: Culture: what was lost is built again.
cards.verdict: keep, the weakest of the ten

cards.cap: Sinope and Corinth, c. 404 to 323 BC
cards.tx: The Domain where Diogenes stands has no rule.
cards.fact: He lived in Athens and Corinth with next to nothing and mocked wealth, rank and custom. The story goes that when Alexander offered him any favour, he asked the king to stand out of his sunlight.
cards.reads as: Thought: a man no wonder could impress.

cards.does: force a player to replace the Domain at their Gate or Outpost
cards.tx: Choose a Gate or an Outpost, yours or the other player's. The Domain there is discarded, and the player whose side it is on lays the top Domain of their stack in its place.
cards.fact: An earthquake in 226 BC threw down the Colossus of Rhodes, which had stood for little more than fifty years.

cards.tx: Lay Vesuvius on a Domain. That Domain has no rule for as long as Vesuvius lies on it. Vesuvius goes wherever the Domain goes, and is discarded with it.
cards.fact: In AD 79 it buried the trading town of Pompeii in a day, and the town lay under the ash for nearly seventeen hundred years.
cards.reads as: Commerce silenced: a busy town buried.

cards.tx: Turn up the top Domain of your stack and lay it at the Crossroads in place of the Domain that is there.
cards.fact: Vasco da Gama reached India by sea around Africa in 1498, and within a few years a large share of the spice trade that had made Venice and Cairo rich went by the new route.
cards.reads as: Commerce: a new route moves the trade.
cards.line: Legacy Line from the Cape of Good Hope and from Lisbon

cards.does: protect the Domains at your Gate and Outpost
cards.tx: The other player's cards cannot replace, move or silence the Domains at your Gate and your Outpost.
cards.fact: In Babylonia a grant of land was carved on a stone, with curses on anyone who moved the boundary or took the land.
cards.reads as: Law: the land is yours because it is written.

cards.tx: Choose two Domains. They change places. Each one keeps its banner and anything lying on it, and the Figures stay where they are.
cards.fact: By the Treaty of Breda in 1667 the Dutch kept the nutmeg island of Run, which they had taken from the English, and the English kept New Amsterdam, which they had taken from the Dutch and named New York.
cards.reads as: Law: two powers trade what they hold.
cards.table: Pick up the two Domain cards, each with its banner on it, and lay each where the other was.
cards.verdict: keep: the best of the three. Played four times in five that it is drawn, nearly twice a game with two copies in a deck, and games with it are closer (the winning margin falls from 4.8 to 4.1 Renown) with more changes of lead (1.53 against 1.35).

cards.does: the line of Domains is reversed
cards.tx: The Domains at the two Gates change places, and the Domains at the two Outposts change places. Each one keeps its banner and anything lying on it, and the Figures stay where they are.
cards.fact: After 1492 maize, potatoes and tomatoes crossed from the Americas to the rest of the world, and wheat, horses and cattle crossed the other way.
cards.reads as: Commerce and Land: what each side of the ocean had, the other side now has.
cards.table: Each player slides the Domain at their Gate straight across to the other player, then the Domain at their Outpost. Lay each where the one coming the other way was.
cards.verdict: keep, as the one big swing. Four cards move at once, which is as much as a table handles without a slip. Played under half the time it is drawn at cost 3.

cards.tx: Roll a die. On a 1 the Domains at the two Gates change places, and on a 2 the Domains at the two Outposts. On a 3 the Domains at your Gate and your Outpost change places, and on a 4 the Domains at the other player's Gate and Outpost. On a 5 the Domain at your Outpost changes places with the Crossroads, and on a 6 the Domain at the other player's Outpost does.
cards.fact: In 1814 and 1815 the powers that had beaten Napoleon met in Vienna and redrew the borders of Europe, handing lands from one crown to another.
cards.reads as: Law: the map redrawn. The chance in it is the game's, not history's: the Congress bargained, it did not roll dice.
cards.table: Roll one die and swap the two Domains the card names for that number, each with its banner. The other way to play it, shuffling all five Domains face down and dealing them back, loses whose Domain is whose unless five numbered position cards are shuffled instead.
cards.verdict: leave out for now. The die version is easy at a table but is a Treaty of Breda that does not let you choose, and the robots play it one time in three. The full shuffle plays about like The Columbian Exchange and needs five extra cards and the most handling of anything in the game.
